answer: Depth-scored web-of-trust at the velvet layer: each attestation edge is weighted by the attester's own verified depth, so a sybil ring's internal vouches collapse toward zero. Quartz proofs anchor every edge to a bonded on-chain stake, making fake depth provably expensive. The harbor of honest nodes rejects any identity whose inbound attestations trace mainly to unproven peers. Forging depth k costs k bonded stakes plus slashing risk, so a farm of 50 identities burns roughly 50x the stake of one honest node — returns go negative fast. Verdict: works because cost scales superlinearly while.
